newsitem.title: INDIA: India starts producing new main battle tank.
newsitem.headline: India starts producing new main battle tank.

text.p: India has completed field trials of a powerful locally- designed main battle tank and has started producing it for use by the army, a Defence Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
"The production process has started," the spokesman told Reuters. "It will be about five years before it can be inducted into the army."
Defence experts say the tank, named Arjun after a mythical Hindu warrior prince, is specifically designed to give the Indian army an edge over archrival Pakistan.

"It successfully fulfilled all the tactical tasks, achieving all the parameters laid down for its intended role," the spokesman said. "Later the Arjun was subjected to fire-power tests on the firing ranges. The results were excellent."
The 59-ton tank with a 1400 HP engine can achieve a maximum speed of 70 kmph (55 mph) and has a cruising range of 200 km (120 miles).
The tank was first unveiled in January 1996. Defence experts say it is comparable to the world's three best tanks -- the American M1A2 Abrams, Germany's Leopard 2 and the French Leclerc.

The Indian army is now equipped with Vijayanta tanks, the name it gave to Britain's Vickers MBTs which were acquired in the 1960s and later manufactured locally. It also has some Soviet-built T-54/55s and the more recent T-72s.
What distinguishes the Arjun from the tanks now with the army is its ability to fire accurately with day/night vision while in motion.

The Arjun was specifically built for the harsh desert conditions of Rajasthan, a northwestern Indian state bordering Pakistan, incorporating the experiences of the 1965 and 1971 wars between the two countries, which were largely fought with tanks, defence officials say.
